rules: Impact: always sounds smaller than it was
Root cause: a system or process gap, never "Dave"
Action items: add a safeguard, not a firing

coes.title: The Typo
coes.story: While debugging billing, an engineer ran a playbook command. A typo removed far more servers than intended. The status page could not update: it was hosted on the affected service.

options: Increased error rates in one region
Storage achieved a temporary state of zen
The tool allowed removing too much capacity too quickly
Make Dave write "I will not typo" 1,000 times
Add minimum-capacity safeguards to the tool

coes.title: We Deleted Ourselves From the Internet
coes.story: A routine maintenance command withdrew our network routes. Every app went dark. Engineers could not badge into the datacenter: the badge system was on the same network.
coes.flavor: We had to bring an angle grinder. Allegedly.

options: An audit tool failed to block a bad command
Decouple physical access from the production network
Move fast and break fewer things

coes.title: BEDLAM-DL3
coes.story: An email went to a 13,000-person distribution list. Hundreds replied-all asking to be removed. Each reply went to 13,000 people. Email stopped working.
coes.flavor: Someone later made a card game about it.

options: Make a card game about it
Moderate posting to lists over 5,000 members

coes.title: The Leap Day
coes.story: On February 29th, new VMs requested certificates valid for one year. The code added 1 to the year. February 29th, next year, does not exist.
coes.flavor: Time is a flat circle with an extra day.

options: A service disruption affecting some customers
Date math did not handle leap years
Test date logic against leap days

coes.title: More Capacity, More Problems
coes.story: We added servers to the streaming fleet. Every server talks to every other server. The new total exceeded the operating system thread limit, and the whole fleet fell over.
coes.flavor: Scaling up made it worse. Classic.

options: Adding capacity pushed servers past the OS thread limit
Use fewer, larger servers and alarm on thread counts
Increase the thread limit to infinity

wrongLines: ✗ That is a blame. We do not blame.
✗ Greg forwarded it to the VP.
